analysis.title: US Growth & Inflation Recap, BoJ on Hold, EUR Too Low, and Canada Has to Deliver
key_insights: US growth is robust across most dimensions except real estate/housing. Cyclical survey indicators point to hot nominal growth, labor signals show cooling but not cracking with U3 low against historical ranges and against NAIRU, and personal consumption is robust even though income growth lags spending.

UBSe expects headline and core inflation to move lower in 1Q27 and 2Q27 because core goods inflation should stop adding to readings and energy base effects will help. Inflation expectations are well contained, with 5y5y inflation swaps in a comfortable range.
Recent equity stress has the equal weight index outperforming the market cap weighted index on a YTD basis.
The desk finds it increasingly unlikely that EURUSD falls below 1.11 or stays there near term. EUR spot flirted with new one-year lows during the ECB press conference and then reversed.

Eurozone macro fundamentals have improved: FY27 GDP estimates were revised higher to almost pre-US-Iran conflict levels, ERZ7 prices about 3 implied hikes versus more than 4 for SFIZ7, OAT stress is off local peaks, and option implied positioning is improving.
The tactical macro implied fair value model shows the recent leg lower in EURUSD is outside what macro pricing implies. Long EURUSD was added to the systematic portfolio on 10/27.

The BoJ left rates unchanged at 1.25% in an 8-to-1 vote. The December hike is nearly confirmed in market pricing at about 21bps, though JPY 1y1y has come off its highs with almost a full 25bps of implied hikes removed.
USDJPY trades in the 157 range and 1m realized volatility has fallen below 6 vols.

Canada August monthly GDP is due with an average analyst estimate of +20bps m/m, which gives +1.64% y/y. That would be the highest y/y reading outside June's 2.1%. The BoC's growth outlook for consumption and fixed investment was rosy, so solid m/m growth matters.
USDCAD at 1.3950 reflects implied spot fair value, which offers less asymmetry for initiating longs.
